tools.name: map_add_feature_field
tools.description: Add a property field (column) to a layer. name cannot be the reserved word fid; type ∈ string/number/boolean; defaultValue is optional (backfills all features). Idempotent: if the field already exists this returns ok with existed=true (no duplicate write, no version bump). Afterward you can bulk-assign values with map_update_features. To add fields to several layers and/or several fields per layer in ONE call, pass fields:[{name,type,defaultValue?}] plus layer_ids:[...] (or a single layer_id); per-layer results come back in that order and one failing layer does not block the rest.

tools.name: map_add_features
tools.description: Add new features to a PostGIS-backed layer (geometry + properties). Call map_get_feature_table first to learn existing fields; property values must match field types, and geometry type must match the layer type (point/line/polygon).

tools.name: map_add_geojson
tools.description: [Plan mode: rejected with code plan_readonly — planning is read-only, nothing lands in the workspace. Declare this data in the plan's research.additions (slotKey + source + license + sizeMb) and let the execution turn do it.] Add a layer from a session file (vector features are ingested into PostGIS; the source GeoJSON is kept as a file snapshot and the layer references the file by file_id). file_path points to a GeoJSON file in the session working directory (internally uses the import flow); file_id is a registered GeoJSON file returned by map_list_files. Provide at least one of them. Inline geojson is no longer supported. Note: the file content must be renderable GeoJSON (features need geometry); for plain JSON use map_import_file to register it as a data file, then process or convert it to GeoJSON. Polygon layers are validity-checked: an invalid polygon (e.g. a self-intersecting boundary) is repaired with ST_MakeValid and reported in geometry_repair when the repair barely moves the shape (area change ≤5%), otherwise nothing is written and the call fails with code invalid_geometry — fix the source geometry and add the layer again. 3D capability is expressed via style: h3 is the main renderer for point layers; column/path/arc/trips/extrusion are set as explicit 3D overrides via style.view3d. When style is passed, the server validates it fully (renderer x geometry match, paint keys, MapLibre rules); invalid styles return 400 with details and no layer is created.

tools.name: map_add_tile_layer
tools.description: Add a raster tile layer to the map (persisted automatically). Supports XYZ tile URLs, WMS services, etc., using {z}/{x}/{y} placeholders in the URL. The layer ID is generated by the server and returned; to adjust opacity, call map_update_layer_style with that ID and renderer.paint[\"raster-opacity\"].

tools.name: map_ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user to make a choice. Two forms: single (question + 2-5 options + allowFreeText) or a batch via `questions: [{key, question, options, allowFreeText?, topic?}]` (1-5 questions, one card). **This tool returns immediately with a pending receipt and your turn ENDS there** (the answer has no time limit): after the card is delivered, stop - **do not add any sentence after this call** (the card takes over the input area and post-call text is not shown; say what you need to say BEFORE the call), do not re-ask, do not guess the answer, do not keep working in this turn. When the user answers, the platform resumes this same thread and delivers the answer; continue the job then. In Plan Mode research put **3-4 questions that would change the whole execution** into ONE batch call - chosen by impact, not by category (study area / scale / time, goal and how \"done\" is measured, data basis and what fetching it costs, deliverable form and precision) - and do not ask trivia you can default and mark as an assumption instead. One follow-up batch (at most 2 questions) is allowed when an answer opened a real branch; never re-ask a key you already asked. Tag a question with its face via `topic` (\"acquisition\" | \"method\" | \"output\") when it fits: the server records that tag on the clarification entry; the faces are coverage hints, they never block the gate. **When the session already ships the data and the method** (a ready-made use case the user opened) ask NOTHING: write the parameters you adopt into the plan's clarification entries as `source=assumed` (each with `topic` and a value) so the user reviews them on the confirmation card. **Give every question 2-5 options**: options[0] is the option you recommend (the card labels it as Recommended) and the rest follow in order of preference. A question asked *without* options has no default to adopt; prefer giving options since the user may pick either the recommendation or another one. Put the REASON for the recommendation inside options[0] itself (one short clause: keep the whole option within ~24 CJK characters / ~40 latin characters - options render as buttons and long text wraps badly); keep the question text to the question itself (<= ~40 characters) and never move the reasoning into it.

tools.name: map_capture_view
tools.description: Capture the current session map as a THROWAWAY image so you can look at your own cartography — call it at the end of a plan run / analysis turn, then open the returned `path` with the built-in view_image tool and judge the picture (are the deliverable layers visible and distinguishable, is anything buried under an opaque layer, are labels colliding, is the study area in frame?). Fix the styles and capture again, 2-3 rounds max. Default framing (`scope=auto`) prefers the plan's study area (`research.area.bbox`); when the study area is only a point, or there is no plan, it falls back to the union bbox of the deliverable layers (the plan's declared outputs), then to the union of the visible layers, then to the session's own map view — the response's `extent_source` says which one was used. The `no_visible_layers` / `no_features_in_extent` / `same_color_as` / `fully_occluded` / `invisible_style` / `too_many_visible_layers` / `extent_too_wide` / `capture_not_ready` checks come back as fast hints, but the image is the authority; `ready` + `timings` tell you whether the map actually reached idle and how long each phase took (a capture that timed out still returns an image, with `capture_not_ready` — that picture may be incomplete, so re-capture before judging). The PNG is written under the session work directory (`<workDir>/.capture/`) and is NEVER registered as a file or layer: it does not appear in the data panel, it is not a deliverable, and reports must not reference it (they build their own static maps). Output is capped at 1024 px per side (default 1024x768).

tools.name: map_copy_layer_to_session
tools.description: Copy a builtin (catalog) layer's data into the current project so it becomes editable. Builtin catalog layers share one global read-only feature set: map_get_feature_table / map_get_layer_info report builtin=true, editable=false, edit_reason=builtin_readonly and a feature_file_id (where the shared features live). Call this tool when the user asks to edit/fix/extend builtin data: it copies every feature into a project-owned file and repoints the layer (style, order, label unchanged); afterwards map_update_features / map_add_feature_field etc. work on that layer. Idempotent — calling it on an already editable layer returns alreadyEditable=true and changes nothing. Layer styles never need this: styling builtin layers is always allowed in place.

tools.name: map_create_chart
tools.description: [Plan mode: rejected with code plan_readonly — planning is read-only, nothing lands in the workspace. Declare this data in the plan's research.additions (slotKey + source + license + sizeMb) and let the execution turn do it.] Create or update an analysis chart (shown in the 'Charts' section of the data panel). First aggregate the data yourself with Python, then pass a compact domain spec (never a raw ECharts option): type ∈ bar|line|area|pie|donut|scatter|radar|funnel|treemap|heatmap|boxplot|combo. Row shapes: value family (bar/line/area/pie/donut/radar/funnel/treemap) [{name,value,series?}]; scatter [{name,x,y,series?}] with x/y as real finite numbers; heatmap [{name,y,value}] where y is the row category label; boxplot [{name,values:[min,q1,median,q3,max]}]; combo [{name,value,series}] with series non-empty. Missing numeric values must drop the row — never pass null for value/x/y (422 with the row index). Small charts pass inline data (≤200 rows); large charts (high-frequency series / big scatter) use data_file in the session working directory (≤5000 rows; JSON array or {data:[...]}; CSV headers: name,value[,series] | name,x,y[,series] | name,y,value | name,min,q1,median,q3,max). combo also takes seriesKinds ([{name,kind:bar|line|area,yAxis?:0|1}], 1-6) and optional yAxes ([{name?,unit?}] ×1-2) for a second axis. Colors: palette ∈ brand|sunset|okabe-ito|brewer-set2|brewer-dark2|brewer-paired|vintage|macarons|roma, or colors = 1-16 hex strings (#RGB/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA; colors wins when both present). Background: background = #RRGGBB + backgroundOpacity 0-1 (default 1) for charts that must sit on a dark basemap or a dark card - a dark background also switches text/axes to the light-on-dark set, and the pinned map card reuses the same pair. Bar direction: orientation ∈ vertical|horizontal (bar only, optional) — omitted = the automatic rule (category labels longer than 10 characters switch to horizontal); an explicit value overrides it, so pass chart_id + {\"type\":\"bar\",\"orientation\":\"horizontal\"} to turn an existing vertical bar (3-character Chinese district names) into a horizontal bar. title ≤80; unit is the value unit; insight is a one-sentence conclusion (required); source marks the origin (layerId+field enables chart-map highlight; radar/heatmap cannot carry layerId) — layerId/fileId must be non-empty real IDs; when the chart has no layer/file origin, omit source entirely (empty-string ids are treated as no source). Unknown spec key *names* (e.g. \"legend\", \"hbar\") are rejected with a 422 listing the allowed keys — never invent fields; an invalid *value* on a style key (palette/colors/background/orientation) is not fatal: it is dropped, the chart renders with defaults, and the drop is listed in the response \"warnings\". Pass chart_id to update an existing chart (get the ID first with map_list_charts); on update, palette/colors are preserved unless you explicitly pass them (pass palette:\"brand\" to reset to the default).

tools.name: map_delete_chart
tools.description: Delete a chart. Use when the user asks to delete a chart.

tools.name: map_delete_feature_field
tools.description: Delete a property field (column) from a layer. Fields referenced by a renderer/label are rejected (409); adjust the style first.

tools.name: map_delete_features
tools.description: Batch-delete features. Two mutually exclusive modes: feature_ids explicit list (≤1000) or condition (up to 5000 hits). Call map_get_feature_table first to confirm the scope before deleting.

tools.name: map_delete_file
tools.description: Delete a file and all layers associated with it. Use when the user says 'delete file <X>'. Requires file_id; call map_list_files first to obtain it.

tools.name: map_export_features
tools.description: Export a PostGIS layer's features to a file in the session working directory (GeoJSON or CSV; shapefile not supported yet) without pulling data into the model context. Returns the file path so you can continue analysis with Python/pandas. Allowed during Plan mode: this only reads existing session data for local verification (it writes a scratch file in the session working directory, never a layer/file row).

tools.name: map_export_pdf
tools.description: Derive a PDF of an already-saved report (HTML/Word/PPT file_id) for download. PDF is an export/download format only: no new file row or report list entry is created. Repeated exports of the same revision reuse the same cached file and URL. Returns {url, file_name, file_size, cached}.

tools.name: map_fit_bounds
tools.description: Zoom the map to the given rectangular bounding box. Bounds format: [west, south, east, north]. Use when the user says 'zoom to this area' or 'view this region'.

tools.name: map_fly_to
tools.description: Fly to a location. Moves the map center to the given longitude/latitude and sets the zoom level. Use when the user says 'fly to Beijing', 'show Shanghai', 'locate...', or 'go to...'. Coordinate format: [lng, lat] (longitude first, latitude second).

tools.name: map_get_builtin
tools.description: Get one built-in catalog entry: license/attribution, coverage, stats, source URLs, and the list of already-prepared regions (previews). Use it to decide whether the user's target area is already available on the platform. `previews[].key` is what you pass to map_import_builtin; `previews[].region` names the covered city/region; `status` is 'ready' or 'pending' and `importable` is false when a payload/license is missing. For scenarios, entryLayers lists the layers the scenario will instantiate.

tools.name: map_get_chart_asset
tools.description: Get the chart's public SVG asset URL, for embedding in an HTML report with ``. The first call generates a public token; the URL for the same chart_id is stable afterwards, so reuse an asset URL already returned earlier in the conversation instead of calling again unless you need a URL for a brand-new chart.

tools.name: map_get_embed_url
tools.description: Get the embed URL of the current session's map, for embedding an interactive map (iframe) in an HTML report. Returns { url, viewport? } - the URL already carries the study-area viewport as ?center=&zoom= (resolved from the plan's research area, else the visible layers' extent, else the session view), so a report opened as-is lands on the study area instead of the world view. You may still override per view: <iframe src=\"URL&center=LNG,LAT&zoom=ZOOM\"> (center/zoom are required by the report skill; the server fills them in when missing and reports a warning).

tools.name: map_get_feature
tools.description: Read a single feature's full attributes and geometry. feature_id comes from the fid in map_get_feature_table (features without a stable id use @row, e.g. @42). By default only attributes and a geometry summary (type/vertex count) are returned; pass include_geometry=true when you need full coordinates for programmatic fixes.

tools.name: map_get_feature_table
tools.description: Paginate through a layer's attribute table (attributes only, no geometry, to save context). Returns column definitions, total row count, current-page row data (fid + attribute values), editability and builtin markers (builtin, editable, edit_reason, feature_file_id). Call this first when the user wants to view/edit attributes, filter rows by condition, or update values in bulk, to learn the fields and fids. Layers with over 10k features/20MB are read-only. Builtin catalog layers are read-only (edit_reason=builtin_readonly): the attribute table is viewable, but to change data call map_copy_layer_to_session first (it copies the shared features into this project).

tools.name: map_get_layer_info
tools.description: Get a layer's full info: geometry type (geometry_type), current renderer + label config, available property fields with statistics (fields, including numeric ranges and unique-value domains), and builtin/editability markers (builtin, editable, edit_reason, feature_file_id). Builtin catalog layers are globally shared and read-only (editable=false, edit_reason=builtin_readonly): their features live under feature_file_id and can be queried/analyzed, but editing data requires map_copy_layer_to_session first; styling them is always allowed. Call this before modifying any style. layer_id prefers the UUID returned by map_list_layers; if you only have a display name/file name, pass it directly (the server resolves it by name automatically). For several layers pass layer_ids:[...] to read them all in ONE call instead of looping one call per layer; the results array keeps the requested order and each entry is identical to a single-layer call. fields is compact statistics: at most 100 fields; numeric fields include min/max and 5 quantiles; string fields include the first 10 unique values; if you need a more detailed distribution, read the workspace data file directly and compute it yourself. Note: if a numeric field's min/max/quantiles contain decimals (e.g. LENGTH 0.003/0.021), it is a float field — categorized does not support float fields (returns 400); use graduated/interpolated instead.

tools.name: map_get_map_state
tools.description: Get the full current map state, including viewport center, zoom level, basemap style, country mask, and custom mask. Call this before modifying a mask or the basemap to understand the current state.

tools.name: map_get_report
tools.description: Read one saved report revision so you can modify it instead of regenerating from memory. Returns artifact_id, format, file_name, file_path and — for Word/PPT — the full DocSpec/DeckSpec used to compile it. Call map_list_files first to find the report file_id. For HTML reports the content file is returned by file_path; edit the file in the sandbox and save a revision with map_save_report + report_id.

tools.name: map_import_builtin
tools.description: [Plan mode: rejected with code plan_readonly — planning is read-only, nothing lands in the workspace. Declare this data in the plan's research.additions (slotKey + source + license + sizeMb) and let the execution turn do it.] Import a built-in catalog item into the current session (shared read-only layers, no storage quota cost). Pass the parent key for datasets that ship as a single payload, or a `<parentKey>-demo-<region>` preview key for a prepared region (recommended — see map_get_builtin). Dataset parents without their own payload return dataset_payload_missing / render_unavailable: pick a preview key instead. Built-in layers are read-only; call map_copy_layer_to_session before editing their features, and remember styling is always allowed in place. After import, the map fits the new data automatically.

tools.name: map_import_file
tools.description: [Plan mode: rejected with code plan_readonly — planning is read-only, nothing lands in the workspace. Declare this data in the plan's research.additions (slotKey + source + license + sizeMb) and let the execution turn do it.] Import a file from the working directory. GeoJSON/JSON files create map layers (vector features are ingested into PostGIS; the source file is kept as a snapshot); CSV/Excel/Text/Markdown/PDF/DOCX/DOC files are registered as data files (shown in the data list, viewable/downloadable, no layer created). Polygon layers are validity-checked: an invalid polygon (e.g. a self-intersecting boundary) is repaired with ST_MakeValid and reported in geometry_repair when the repair barely moves the shape (area change ≤5%), otherwise the whole file is rejected with code invalid_geometry and zero features are written — fix the source geometry and import again. After importing, call map_get_layer_info to get geometry_type and fields, then use map_update_layer_style to set the appropriate renderer and labels.

tools.name: map_import_image
tools.description: [Plan mode: rejected with code plan_readonly — planning is read-only, nothing lands in the workspace. Declare this data in the plan's research.additions (slotKey + source + license + sizeMb) and let the execution turn do it.] Import a GeoTIFF image file as a map tile layer (auto-converted to COG and persisted). For AI-generated .tif/.tiff files pass file_path directly (no registration needed); for uploaded files pass file_id. Provide exactly one of file_path or file_id.

tools.name: map_layout_checkpoint
tools.description: Create an immutable saved version from the current layout draft. Use map_layout_freeze for a publication snapshot with frozen map/data resources.

tools.name: map_layout_create
tools.description: Create a Live Atlas layout from a valid MapLayoutSpec or a deterministic built-in template. Provide template_id for the normal path, or a complete spec for an imported layout. The server validates the complete spec and rejects arbitrary HTML/CSS/JS.

tools.name: map_layout_freeze
tools.description: Freeze the current draft into a publication snapshot. Map frames are captured by the open MapX Agent workspace because WebGL map rendering cannot be reconstructed in the API process; the tool waits for that browser capture to finish. Use a fresh expected_revision.

tools.name: map_layout_get
tools.description: Read one Live Atlas layout: mutable draft, immutable versions, freeze snapshots, bindings, variants, and provenance.

tools.name: map_layout_list
tools.description: List saved Live Atlas layouts in this session. Use it before creating a duplicate or before choosing a layout to inspect/render.

tools.name: map_layout_manage
tools.description: Manage a layout without editing its content: rename, duplicate, archive, unarchive, delete, restore a saved version, apply a deterministic built-in or team template, or undo a recent structured operation. Publishing and approval remain human-only.

tools.name: map_layout_preview
tools.description: Evaluate the latest live draft before freezing: run draft proof and render a temporary low-resolution PNG through the open workspace. This creates no version and no file-panel asset. Open the returned path with view_image, fix the draft if needed, and freeze only after the preview and proof are acceptable.

tools.name: map_layout_proof
tools.description: Run the shared cartographic proof engine. Omit version_id to evaluate the latest live draft without freezing or persisting a proof; provide version_id only when auditing an immutable release version. Draft proof never probes the optional print runtime.

tools.name: map_layout_render
tools.description: Render a frozen layout version to PNG/JPEG/SVG/PDF. A live draft must be frozen first. Supports FOGRA39 PDF/X-4 structural validation and returns an artifact path.

tools.name: map_layout_templates
tools.description: List built-in professional layout templates with their page ratio and intended use. Call this before creating a layout from a named template.

tools.name: map_layout_update
tools.description: Apply a transaction of structured LayoutOperations to a layout draft. Supports insert, remove, updateFrame, updateItem, reorder, page, master, setBinding, setConstraints, setVariantOverride, setGeoRelation, removeGeoRelation and batch. These operations cover every editable Studio surface, including map cameras/layers, text/content/style, frames, visibility, lock, charts, tables, bindings and layout variants. Use the layout's current draftRevision as expected_revision. Frozen items and source provenance are protected by the server. Returns a compact receipt with the new revision; use map_layout_get only when the full spec is needed. Retry with a new idempotency key after a revision conflict.

tools.name: map_list_assets
tools.description: List all data assets in the session (spatial layers + data files, deduplicated). Each asset is labeled with its type (layer/file) and name. More user-friendly than map_list_layers.

tools.name: map_list_builtin
tools.description: List the platform's built-in data catalog (curated datasets such as population, DEM, GDP, land cover, roads, buildings, hazard and air-quality layers). ALWAYS call this before downloading data from the internet: the platform has already prepared one or more regions per dataset, and importing a built-in item is instant and free. Each item returns key/kind/name/domain/geometryType/volumeMb/status/importable/blockReason plus previewRegions (the regions already prepared as `<parentKey>-demo-<region>` keys). Filters: query (matches key, names AND prepared regions - search the city name, e.g. \"jakarta\"), domain (the dataset's subject: terrain-surface/water-watershed/climate-ecology/hazard-environment/population-settlement/facility-transport/economy-industry/boundary-governance), industry, use_case, kind (dataset|scenario|all), importable_only, limit (default 20, max 100), offset. Next step: call map_get_builtin for the candidate key to see its prepared regions, then map_import_builtin with a preview key; only download from upstream when no prepared region matches the user's area (see the geodata-download skill).

tools.name: map_list_charts
tools.description: List all charts in the session (returns only ID/name/type/row count/insight/source/pin status, no data, to save context). Call this before modifying a chart to get the chart_id.

tools.name: map_list_files
tools.description: List all files in the session (uploaded data files and AI-generated intermediate files). Returns file_id, file_name, file_type, file_size, columns, etc.

tools.name: map_list_layers
tools.description: List all layers currently on the map (ID, name, type, visibility). Use map_list_assets for a data-asset view that includes file information.

tools.name: map_list_mcp_tools
tools.description: List all external MCP connections enabled for the current user with their full tool catalogs (tool names + descriptions), and give the actual callable name of each tool in the codex session (prefixed with umcp_<ID>__). Call this first when the user references an MCP tool (e.g. mapbox's isochrone_tool) or when you need to confirm which tools a given MCP exposes; then call the returned callable_name. Do not use list_mcp_resources / list_mcp_resource_templates to determine tool availability — they only list resources, not tools.

tools.name: map_move_layer_down
tools.description: Move a layer down one position. Use when the user says 'move <X> down' or 'put <X> below'.

tools.name: map_move_layer_up
tools.description: Move a layer up one position. Use when the user says 'move <X> up' or 'put <X> above'.

tools.name: map_pan
tools.description: Pan the map in a given direction. Use when the user says 'move north', 'look right', or 'fly west'.

tools.name: map_patch_report
tools.description: Apply targeted semantic edits to an existing Word or PPT report and compile a new immutable revision of the same artifact. Prefer this over re-saving the full spec for localized changes; for structural rewrites use map_save_word_report / map_save_presentation with report_id. Ops: set_title {title}; set_subtitle {subtitle|null}; set_date {date|null}; set_author {author|null} (PPT, deck-level cover author; null clears it); replace_text {scope:{kind:'title'|'subtitle'|'date'|'message'|'section_text'|'slide_text'|'table_cell', ...}, new}; set_slide {slide, title?/message?/bullets?/note?}; set_slide_media {slide, media|null}; insert_section/remove_section/move_section {section|index...}; add_slide/duplicate_slide/remove_slide/move_slide {slide, to?...}; set_theme {theme:{...}} (PPT). Ambiguous or missing targets return a clear error instead of guessing.

tools.name: map_pin_chart
tools.description: Pin a chart to the map or unpin it. Pinning is additive: a session can carry several pinned cards at once (2-4 read well; unpin the ones you no longer need with pinned:false) and unpinning one keeps the others. layout is optional: x/y are proportions of the map viewport (0-1, e.g. bottom-right x=0.65,y=0.7), w/h are the card's pixel width/height (w 280-1200, h optional 220-1200); when layout is omitted, the existing layout is kept or a cascade default is used (each new card is nudged down-right so it does not sit exactly on the previous one).

tools.name: map_prune_intermediate_layers
tools.description: Delete ALL intermediate layers of this session in one call: analysis intermediates (displayPending), workflow step products marked display=none, and hidden products left behind by superseded runs of the same plan. Deliverable layers, layers referenced by a chart and shared originals are kept. Pass no ids — the target set is recomputed server-side from that rule (the same rule the layer panel's 'delete all intermediate layers' button uses). Use when the user asks to clean up / tidy the intermediate layers, and report the deleted and kept counts.

tools.name: map_query_features
tools.description: Query features of a PostGIS-backed layer with structured filters. Token-safe by design: default 50 rows (max 5000), cells truncated to 200 chars, geometry excluded unless with_geometry=true (then capped at 100 rows). Prefer aggregate mode (count / distinct / stats) over fetching raw rows, and map_export_features for large result sets so data goes to a file instead of context. condition ops: eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/in/contains (single op per call — for range filters like 1<x<5 make two aggregate calls or use map_query_sql). stats returns count/min/max/avg/sum. Builtin catalog layers (map_list_layers / map_get_layer_info report builtin=true) are read-only and their features live under feature_file_id: querying/analysis works as usual, but editing them requires map_copy_layer_to_session first.

tools.name: map_query_sql
tools.description: Execute an arbitrary read-only SQL query scoped to the CURRENT session's platform data (SELECT/WITH/EXPLAIN only). This is for the platform's own layer/feature data; for a database the USER connected (MySQL/PostgreSQL data source) use db_query instead — do not use this tool for those. Queryable relations are exactly three session-scoped read-only views, whose column names mirror the underlying tables: session_features (= vector_features: id, fid, file_id, geom, area_m2, vertex_count, properties), session_files (= file: id, \"sessionId\", \"fileName\", \"fileType\", \"filePath\", \"fileSize\", columns, source, role, …), session_layers (= layer: id, \"sessionId\", type, label, data, style, \"order\", visible, \"fileId\", storage, …). The base tables (vector_features / file / layer / business_session) are NOT queryable — other sessions' and other users' rows are unreachable by design, so do not try to enumerate them; use map_list_layers / map_list_files / map_get_layer_info for metadata instead. Results are capped (default 50 rows, max 5000) and cells truncated (default 200 chars) to protect context. Raw geometry columns (geom) are returned as compact summaries ({type, bbox, pointCount}) — avoid SELECT * on session_features; select only needed columns/properties and use map_export_features for raw geometry/large exports. Prefer map_query_features with aggregate/condition for simple counts and stats. Schema contract: session_features has NO layer_id column — rows belong to a file (columns: file_id, fid, geom, properties); a layer references its data file via layer.\"fileId\" (session_layers columns: id, \"sessionId\", \"fileId\"). To filter session_features by a layer, either read the layer's file_id from map_list_layers and use WHERE file_id = '<file_id>', or join: WHERE vf.file_id = (SELECT l.\"fileId\" FROM session_layers l WHERE l.id = '<layer_id>'). Builtin shared layers (map_get_layer_info reports builtin / feature_file_id) keep their features under that canonical feature_file_id, which is exactly session_features.file_id — filter by it as usual. Two Postgres gotchas worth knowing before you write the query (each mismatch costs a retry): one statement only — a single trailing semicolon is fine, but two statements separated by ';' are rejected; and round(x, n) exists only for numeric, so cast the input (`round(ST_Area(geom::geography)/1e6::numeric, 1)`), never `round(double precision, integer)`. Queries that reference session_features.layer_id, or that touch a non-session relation, are rejected with actionable guidance.

tools.name: map_raster_stats
tools.description: Read a raster layer's REAL file statistics (not the renderer range): pixel size (width/height/cells), band count, data type, and band min/max/mean/stddev/nodata. Use this to decide whether a raster actually carries signal in the study area BEFORE running analysis on it — a layer whose renderer min/max reads 0/0 may just have a stale or missing style range (map_get_layer_info's min/max comes from the renderer/style, not the file). `constant: true` means every valid pixel has the same value (e.g. an all-zero payload), which makes the layer useless as an analysis factor — report it to the user instead of silently producing a flat result. The result is cached back into layer.data.bandStats so the style editor and the whole-raster legend pick up the true range. Only raster layers are supported (vector layers return not_raster). layer_id prefers the UUID from map_list_layers; a display name also resolves.

tools.name: map_refresh_layer_data
tools.description: Re-parse a layer's data file and refresh the platform (recompute column metadata, clear caches, broadcast workspace/embed). For batch computed edits (e.g. assigning values to thousands of rows by rule or cleaning fields), the token-cheapest approach: edit the GeoJSON with Python directly in the session working directory (top-level features array; feature.id may be kept/added), then call this tool to validate, persist, and refresh.

tools.name: map_remove_layer
tools.description: Remove a layer from the map. Use when the user says 'delete layer <X>' or 'remove the previous result'. layer_id must be the UUID returned by map_list_layers — never use a display name or file name.

tools.name: map_rename_layer
tools.description: Rename a layer. Use when the user says 'rename layer' or 'rename <X> to <Y>'. layer_id must be the UUID returned by map_list_layers — never use a display name or file name.

tools.name: map_reorder_layers
tools.description: Reorder layers in the given order (first = topmost); the backend persists atomically and broadcasts to the platform and live pages. Two modes: mode=\"subset\" (recommended for delivery tidy-up) moves just the listed layers to the top in the given order and keeps every other layer's relative order — pass your deliverable layer ids only; mode=\"permutation\" (default, legacy) requires the complete array of ALL current layer UUIDs. Use when the user asks to 'put <X> on top/bottom' or 'arrange layers in <X> order'; for single-step moves still use map_move_layer_up / map_move_layer_down.

tools.name: map_save_presentation
tools.description: Save a native, editable PowerPoint (.pptx) deck (16:9) (or a new revision of an existing one). Use when the user asks for a PPT/presentation/slide deck. Author a DeckSpec designed for one message per slide: deck.slides[] entries have layout (cover|agenda|title-bullets|visual-right|visual-full|data-table|big-number|quote|two-column|timeline|close), title, an optional one-sentence message, bullets (aim for ≤5, hard cap 8), layout payloads: big-number takes stats:[{label,value,note?}] (1-4), two-column takes columns:[{heading?,bullets[]}] (exactly 2), timeline takes items:[{label,text?}] (2-6), quote renders the message as a large pull-quote, an optional media (map embed URL with center/zoom or chart asset URL; at most one visual per slide), optional table, and note (speaker notes). deck.title/subtitle/date plus an optional deck.author (plain name shown on the cover) are deck-level cover fields; cover/close slides render deck-level text rather than their own title/bullets. deck.theme is optional and takes six-digit hex colors without '#' (primary/accent/ink/muted/paper/coverBackground/coverText); see the presentation-generation skill for the full theme contract. The server compiles the deck deterministically; charts become PNGs and maps become static screenshots. Pass an existing pptx file_id as report_id to create a revision; for targeted edits prefer map_patch_report. deck must be passed directly as the JSON object value of the top-level deck key — never wrap parameters under an arguments key and never serialize deck to a JSON string.

tools.name: map_save_report
tools.description: [Plan mode: rejected with code plan_readonly — planning is read-only, nothing lands in the workspace. Declare this data in the plan's research.additions (slotKey + source + license + sizeMb) and let the execution turn do it.] Save an LLM-generated HTML analysis report (or a new revision of an existing HTML report). Only for HTML reports — cannot be used to register imagery or other data files (for GeoTIFF use map_import_image with file_path). First write the HTML to the session working directory with the shell (e.g. cat > report.html), then pass file_path (relative paths resolve against the session working directory; absolute paths also accepted). To modify an existing HTML report pass its file_id as report_id: a new immutable revision is created and the report list/artifacts keep them grouped.

tools.name: map_save_word_report
tools.description: Save a professional, editable Word (.docx) report (or a new revision of an existing one). Use when the user asks for a Word report, an editable document version, or a consulting-grade written deliverable. Author content as a structured DocSpec: doc.sections[] entries carry heading (1-3), paragraphs, bullets, numbered, table (headers+rows), an optional media (map embed URL with center/zoom, or chart asset URL), and note. The server compiles the .docx deterministically; charts become PNGs and map embeds become static map screenshots. Pass an existing docx file_id as report_id to create a revision; for targeted edits prefer map_patch_report. doc must be passed directly as the JSON object value of the top-level doc key — never wrap parameters under an arguments key and never serialize doc to a JSON string.

tools.name: map_set_basemap_category
tools.description: Set the color and/or visibility of a basemap category. Supports 8 categories: background, water, green, roads, buildings, aeroway, boundaries, labels. Use when the user says 'make the water dark blue' or 'hide the roads'. The current basemap style and visibility can be inspected with the map_get_map_state tool.

tools.name: map_set_basemap_style
tools.description: Switch the basemap style. 5 options: positron (light gray), positronWithLabels (light gray + labels), dark (dark), darkWithLabels (dark + labels), none (no basemap, plain white). Use when the user says 'switch to the dark basemap', 'remove basemap labels', 'hide the basemap', or 'change the basemap style'.

tools.name: map_set_country_mask
tools.description: Clip the basemap to a country/region. Only the basemap inside the given country is shown; the rest is covered with a background color. Pass an empty string to remove the mask and restore the full map.

tools.name: map_set_custom_mask
tools.description: Clip the basemap to a custom GeoJSON extent. Pass an empty string to remove the mask.

tools.name: map_set_layer_visibility
tools.description: [Plan mode: rejected with code plan_readonly — planning is read-only, nothing lands in the workspace. Declare this data in the plan's research.additions (slotKey + source + license + sizeMb) and let the execution turn do it.] Toggle one or many layers' visibility (show/hide). Use when the user says 'hide layer <X>' or 'show layer <X>'. layer_id / layer_ids must be UUIDs returned by map_list_layers — never a display name or file name. Pass layer_ids:[...] to show/hide a whole batch in ONE call (hiding 30 intermediates one by one costs 30 round trips — do not loop). Turning ON a deferred analysis product also PUBLISHES it (the platform lazily builds its display artifact and moves it out of the `intermediate analysis products` group), so this is the call to use when the user should see a raster result. Before your final answer, hide the intermediate layers you created for this turn and leave only the deliverable visible.

tools.name: map_set_terrain
tools.description: Enable/disable 3D terrain (requires a DEM source URL, raster-dem tile template). Only takes effect in 3D mode.

tools.name: map_set_view_mode
tools.description: Switch between 2D/3D view mode. 3D mode: tilted camera (default pitch=60), sky, automatic extrusion of polygon layers into 3D bodies and point layers into 3D columns; 2D mode restores the flat view. mode is required (2d/3d); pitch/bearing/sky/terrain are optional. Use when the user says 'switch to 3D', 'show the 3D effect', or 'back to 2D'.

tools.name: map_update_features
tools.description: Batch-update feature attributes (and optionally replace the whole geometry). Two mutually exclusive modes: (1) updates explicit list (≤1000 items; each feature_id + partial-merge properties + optional geometry); (2) condition + properties (batch-edit values by field condition, up to 5000 hits). feature_id must be the platform's own id (`fid` from map_query_features / map_get_feature_table / map_get_layer_info) — ids from a locally exported file or from the original source data do NOT resolve and return 404 (re-query the fids first, or match by a condition instead). Attribute values must match the field types; for unknown fields call map_add_feature_field first (adding an existing field is a no-op success). Changing geometry is only for programmatic fixes (e.g. snapping to a grid); for vertex-level editing ask the user to do it in the UI.

tools.name: map_update_layer_style
tools.description: Modify a layer's renderer, labels, legend, layer-level symbols, and 3D height override. For the JSON schema load the styles skill; for delivery-grade judgement (layer order, polygon opacity so stacked fills do not bury each other, one hue per theme, blind-spot backdrops, legends, labels) load the deliverable-cartography skill. The main renderer is the 2D semantic style (3D auto-projects by default; switch 2D/3D with map_set_view_mode); view3d only allows the height triplet {heightField,height,heightScale} or null (null clears the height override); symbol is the layer-level symbol (null clears it); per-category symbols are written inside the renderer. renderer/label/legend must not be null (disable labels/legend with {\"enabled\":false}). To set the whole-layer opacity of a categorized / graduated / interpolated / multi_field vector layer, set renderer.opacity (0-1, default 1, 0 = fully invisible) in ONE field: it is multiplied onto the per-category/range/stop opacity at compile time, so the class-level values are never rewritten and stay individually adjustable. Never rewrite categories[] / ranges[] / stops[] just to change the whole layer's opacity, and do not add an opacity field to single/deck renderer types (single already carries layer-level opacity in its paint). The server fully validates renderer/label/legend/view3d/symbol (renderer x geometry match, paint-key whitelist, MapLibre expression rules); invalid input returns 400 with details (per-item path + reason + suggestion) and is not persisted — fix per the details and retry; returns changed:false when the style is unchanged. categorized category values only allow strings or integer numbers: float fields/float categories are rejected (use graduated/interpolated instead). For graduated renderers, range from/to values should lie within the target field's data domain (query map_get_layer_info for min/max/domain); out-of-domain boundaries are accepted with warnings and matching features fall back to the default style. layer_id / layer_ids must be UUIDs returned by map_list_layers; pass layer_ids:[...] to apply the SAME style to a batch in one call instead of looping. When each layer needs a DIFFERENT style, pass styles:[{layer_id,style},...] to apply them all in ONE call (still exactly one of layer_id / layer_ids / styles); per-layer validation failures are reported per layer and do not roll back the others. Restyling an EXISTING layer is always IN PLACE on that layer_id: never create a copy layer to carry a style, never run an operator step (select_features / buffer / ...) that just reproduces the layer, and never hide the layer the user referred to. This in-place restyle is allowed even while Plan Mode is on - the Plan Mode toggle does NOT force a plan for a simple restyle.

tools.name: map_zoom_in
tools.description: Zoom the map in by one level. Use when the user says 'zoom in' or 'get closer'. Use the times parameter to zoom multiple levels.

tools.name: map_zoom_out
tools.description: Zoom the map out by one level. Use when the user says 'zoom out' or 'move farther away'. Use the times parameter to zoom multiple levels.

tools.name: map_zoom_to_layer
tools.description: Zoom the map to a layer's extent so all of its content is fully visible in the viewport. Use when the user says 'zoom to <layer>' or 'locate <layer>'. Requires layer_id; call map_list_layers first to obtain it.
